title: BART inspector general funding and spending
question: What portion of the new funding did oversight use, and do published cost totals reconcile?
finding: FY2026 category amounts add to $2,139,566, or 79.2% of the $2.7 million budget. The $437,084 consulting total already includes all seven listed projects.
how: Compare the 2022 grand jury and board response, the June 2023 funding proposal and the FY2025, FY2026 midyear and FY2026 year-end reports. Add each annual cost category once.
limits: Spending below a budget does not itself establish loss, inadequate oversight, a returned appropriation or misconduct.

rows.test: How did BART propose to fund independent oversight after a grand jury sought at least $2.7 million a year?
rows.record: In 2022 BART answered that a peer-agency funding recommendation was unimplemented. In June 2023 toll authority staff proposed $2.1 million annually from BATA and $600,000 from BART. The proposed $11.6 million amendment comprised $1.1 million more in FY2023–24 and five later years at $2.1 million. The proposed total agreement ceiling was $16.6 million. FY2025 and FY2026 reports subsequently give the office an annual $2.7 million budget.
rows.limit: The proposed ten-year agreement ceiling spans prior funding and future annual appropriations. It does not measure annual or cumulative cash payments.

source.t: Alameda County 2021–22 grand jury report, PDF page 131

comparison.t: BART response to recommendation 60, PDF page 6

payment.t: Toll authority funding amendment staff report, PDF pages 25–27

rows.test: Does the inspector’s annual spending reconcile to the budget and the individual cost categories?
rows.record: The FY2025 report put spending just below $2.2 million on a $2.7 million budget. In FY2026 the five reported categories totaled $2,139,566, or 79.2% of the $2.7 million budget. Workforce cost was $1,579,280 and consulting was $437,084. The earlier semiannual report put spending at about 35% midway through the year, and anticipated invoices later in the year.
rows.limit: The arithmetic difference of $560,434 is budget authority above FY2026 reported expenditures. An actual return, committed balance or lost service would require the year-end appropriation and encumbrance records.

source.t: FY2026 annual expenditure table and consultant projects, PDF page 14

comparison.t: FY2026 midyear spending and expected timing, PDF page 9

payment.t: FY2025 spending beside the following year’s planned budget, PDF page 9

rows.test: Should the individual consulting and investigation amounts be added on top of total spending?
rows.record: Seven FY2026 project rows sum to $437,084 exactly, the consulting category already included in $2,139,566. The $67,826 witness-retaliation investigation and $17,344 attorney-representation rows are included in that subtotal. The separate multi-year project values include prior fiscal years.
rows.limit: The annual report does not identify a specific witness, a finding of retaliation or an improper invoice from these aggregate line items.
